item.title: Forum on overseas studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era held in Budapest
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
Participants attend an academic seminar at the Hungarian thematic forum of the 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in Budapest, Hungary, Nov. 21, 2026. (Xinhua/Hu Zhixuan) BUDAPEST, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The Hungarian thematic forum of the 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era was held in Budapest on Saturday. The forum was co-hosted by the Institute of European Studies of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the China-CEE Institute under the theme "Mutual Trust, Interconnection and Shared Benefits: the Vision of a Community with a Shared Future for Humanity and China-Europe Cooperation for Mutual Benefits." Experts and scholars from China and several European countries attended the forum, discussing topics including the global significance of Chinese modernization, the vision of a community with a shared future for humanity and China-Europe cooperation. Hungary was the first European country to sign a cooperation document with China on the Belt and Road Initiative. Strengthening dialogue and cooperation between China and Europe is an important way to put the vision of a community with a shared future for humanity into practice and help translate the four major global initiatives into concrete results in addressing shared challenges, they said. Connectivity is a practical means through which the vision of a community with a shared future for humanity takes tangible form, they said. ■ Participants attend the Hungarian thematic forum of the 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in Budapest, Hungary, Nov. 21, 2026. (Xinhua/Hu Zhixuan)

item.title: Asia-Pacific Media Partnership officially launched
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The Asia-Pacific Media Partnership (APMP), proposed by China's Xinhua News Agency, has been officially launched, with its first batch of members comprising 310 organizations from 41 countries and regions across the Asia-Pacific. At the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Media Forum held on Sept. 5, more than 400 representatives from over 40 countries and regions, as well as from UN agencies and international organizations, witnessed the establishment of the Organizing Committee of the Asia-Pacific Media Partnership Program. The committee issued an initiative on strengthening collaborative communication between the media and think tanks, inviting media outlets and think tanks in the Asia-Pacific region to join the partnership. Aiming to strengthen mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation among media organizations across the Asia-Pacific region, the APMP focuses on building four key platforms: high-end dialogue, collaborative communication, technological innovation and pragmatic cooperation. It will regularly hold high-level media dialogues, promote joint interviews among Asia-Pacific media, jointly produce high-quality multimedia products, organize inbound reporting tours in China for Asia-Pacific media journalists, and host themed training programs for Asia-Pacific media professionals, among a series of practical cooperation projects. Both the APMP and the Shenzhen Consensus of the Asia-Pacific Media Forum have been officially included in the deliverables list for China's hosting of the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meetings. The Asia-Pacific Media Forum has also been included in the list of meetings and events hosted by China as the 2026 APEC host. ■

item.title: Roundup: One-China principle unshakable, DPP's "Taiwan independence" attempts doomed to fail: experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The recent meeting between the heads of state of China and the United States and the China-Russia-U.S. summit have sent a clear message: the Taiwan question is at the heart of China's core interests and the international community's commitment to the one-China principle is unshakable, experts and scholars across the Taiwan Strait said. They said the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities' attempts to seek "Taiwan independence" by relying on external forces and military buildup are doomed to fail. On Nov. 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping met with U.S. President Donald Trump, who was in the southern Chinese metropolis of Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting. Xi also hosted a historic summit with Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the same day. During his meeting with Trump, Xi said that on the Taiwan question, the U.S. side should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-U.S. relations. Trump, for his part, said the United States does not support "Taiwan independence." Chen Guiqing, a research fellow at the Beijing-based Institute of Taiwan Studies, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, said Xi had once again made China's firm position on the Taiwan question clear to the United States while also setting out China's expectations. The Taiwan question concerns not only the overall stability of China-U.S. relations but also global stability, Chen said. Doing the right thing means, among other things, that the United States should stop playing the "Taiwan card" and refrain from sending wrong signals to secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," he said. Otherwise, it will affect efforts by the two countries to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability, Chen added. Ni Yongjie, director of the Shanghai Institute of Taiwan Studies, noted that this was the first time during Trump's presidency that he had publicly stated at a meeting between the two heads of state that the United States does not support "Taiwan independence." The statement represented a response by the U.S. side to China's major concerns over the Taiwan question, Ni said. Experts said the Taiwan-related positions articulated by the two leaders dealt another heavy blow to secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence." Chang Chun-kai, a research fellow at the Center for Cross-Strait Political and Economic Studies, Chengchi University, said the one-China principle constitutes the political foundation of China-U.S. relations and is indispensable to ensuring peace and stability. Peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait depend on the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, Chang said, adding that this is also in line with the broader trend toward a stable relationship between China and the United States. The Taiwan question stems from China's civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war, combined with foreign interference, has kept the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. At the trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump, Xi stressed that countries should not interfere in one another's domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs. On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another, Xi said. Putin said the three countries should adhere to the principles of sovereign equality and noninterference in internal affairs, and look for ways to resolve concerns in a balanced manner through cooperation. Li Huan, a research fellow at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations, said the summit carries an important message for the Taiwan question: major countries are willing to sit down and communicate directly to manage differences and avoid misjudgment and conflict, which shatters the attempt and illusion of secessionist forces to exploit competition among major countries to pursue "Taiwan independence." Commenting on Trump's statement and the consensus reached by the three heads of state, Chen said that although secessionist forces on the island are trying to downplay their significance, more and more people in Taiwan will come to see clearly that "Taiwan independence" attempts find no support and will never succeed. Xi noted at the summit that, as the main victors of World War II, China, Russia and the United States should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and defend the hard-won outcomes of victory in World War II. Li said Taiwan's restoration to China was one of the outcomes of victory in World War II and an important part of the postwar international order, adding that the historical and legal fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China is clear and indisputable. By recalling the three countries' history of fighting side by side during World War II and reaffirming their commitment to safeguarding the postwar international order and the purposes of the UN Charter, the summit sent a stern warning to forces seeking to challenge that order and undermine the achievements of the war, including secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," she said. Feng Wang, a Taiwan-based history writer, said the history of World War II and the victory over fascism were shared historical memories of the international community that must neither be forgotten nor distorted. People in Taiwan should not be misled by political manipulation or erroneous views of history, Wang said, adding that people from all walks of life in Taiwan should take a long-term and broad view, thinking in the direction that benefits Taiwan compatriots, the country and the Chinese nation. "Secession aimed at 'Taiwan independence' is the root cause of turmoil across the Taiwan Strait. It harms the immediate interests of people on both sides of the Strait and is widely opposed by the international community. It is a dead end," Ni said. The DPP authorities should abandon their secessionist stance as soon as possible and return to the path of peaceful development of cross-Strait relations, he added. ■

item.title: Forum on overseas studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era held in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 21, 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei) BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era opened in Beijing on Saturday. Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony. Participants said Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era had taken shape and evolved through efforts to respond to questions posed by China, by the world, by the people, and by the times, and to advance China's development in tandem with that of the rest of the world. They noted that Xi has proposed the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity, offering China's answer to common challenges facing countries in the current era and has won broad recognition from the international community. Participants called for stronger overseas research into and communication of the Thought, as well as joint efforts to advance global development, safeguard world peace and stability, promote human progress and improve the global governance system. Under the theme "The Great Way: Building a Community with a Shared Future for Humanity," the forum was hosted by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. It will run through Sunday, with thematic sessions also being held in Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and five countries, namely Uzbekistan, Ethiopia, Greece, Hungary and Uruguay, bringing together nearly 650 participants from more than 80 countries and regions. ■

item.title: Xinhua Headlines: Why China-Russia-U.S. summit hailed historic for world stability, peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- World leaders and observers spoke highly of the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States, saying the talks have brought the world hope for peace, stability and cooperation. Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired the historic summit in the city of Shenzhen, south China, on Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump. As major countries and permanent members of the UN Security Council, China, Russia and the United States should set good examples, work together to meet global challenges, jointly uphold world peace and stability, and make greater contributions to the progress of humanity, Xi said. Following the summit, the three countries released the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, outlining their common understandings on issues including the UN reform, energy security, the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court and nuclear risk reduction. LANDMARK STEP FOR GLOBAL SECURITY At a White House news conference on Friday, Trump hailed the Shenzhen meeting as "one of the most momentous international summits in many years." He said the "historic summit" had produced a trilateral peace declaration in which China, Russia and the United States reaffirmed that a nuclear war must never be fought. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said China's efforts to host the summit will help create and open up space for meaningful dialogue and mutual understanding toward lasting peace and harmony. Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said the three leaders had shown wisdom and statesmanship in taking a step that mattered to the wider international community. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico said he noticed how often the leaders had spoken of peace during their meeting. At the United Nations, Farhan Haq, deputy spokesman for the secretary-general, said the organization welcomed efforts by world leaders, including those of the Security Council's permanent members, to seek common solutions to global problems. Denis Simon, former executive vice chancellor of Duke Kunshan University, said the summit could open a new channel for dialogue on international security among the three countries whose decisions carry considerable military, economic and diplomatic weight. "I see the meeting as an important opening," said Paul Frimpong, executive director of the Africa-China Center for Policy and Advisory. With several international crises unfolding at once, he said, sitting together gave each leader a chance to hear directly from the other two about the risks they considered most pressing and where they saw room to act together. Gergely Salat, a senior researcher at the Hungarian Institute of International Affairs, said the meeting showed that China has been maintaining channels with both Washington and Moscow and has enough credibility with both to bring them to the same table. "Few capitals could do that today," he said. FINDING RIGHT WAY TO GET ALONG At the summit, Xi made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. "China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means," he said. Sourabh Gupta, a resident senior fellow at the Institute for China-America Studies in Washington, noted the repeated references at the summit to preserving the outcomes of World War II. As permanent members of the UN Security Council, the three countries bear a special responsibility for maintaining international peace and security, he said. Wang Yiwei, a professor at Renmin University of China's School of International Studies, said advances in artificial intelligence were adding a new layer of risk for nuclear powers. Against that backdrop, he said, China's emphasis on preserving strategic stability at the summit sent an encouraging signal about the prospects for peace. Shraga Biran, head of Israel's Institute for Structural Reforms, pointed to the Middle East, noting that with several regional flashpoints in play, reliable communication can keep one miscalculation from triggering another and reduce the risk that a crisis escalates by accident. ENCOURAGING CONSENSUS Xi called on the three countries to follow through on the consensus reached at the summit, strengthen communication, build common ground through dialogue, promote peace via cooperation, and work together to build a better world. Ezzat Saad, director of the Cairo-based Egyptian Council for Foreign Affairs, said that a better understanding among the major countries could give diplomats more room to work and help contain tensions across the Middle East region. "When fuel and freight costs rise, businesses pay more to move goods, and families can feel it in food prices," said Frimpong with the Africa-China Center for Policy and Advisory. In the heads of state declaration released following the summit, the three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows. In regions recovering from conflict, Frimpong said, more reliable energy supplies would also make it easier for businesses to reopen and invest. For Alphonse Muleefu, principal of the College of Arts and Social Sciences at the University of Rwanda, the declaration issued in Shenzhen showed that the three countries could find common ground. Building on it, he said, would take mutual respect, sustained dialogue and practical cooperation. "I believe this meeting marks an encouraging step toward a more stable world," he said.■

item.title: China's high-tech FDI posts strong growth in first 10 months
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
BEIJING, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Foreign direct investment (FDI) in China's high-tech industries posted robust year-on-year growth in the first 10 months of 2026, official data showed on Friday. FDI in high-tech industries reached 252.83 billion yuan (about 37.66 billion U.S. dollars) during the January-October period, up 31.3 percent year on year. It accounted for 41.7 percent of China's total FDI in actual use, increasing by 10.7 percentage points from the same period last year, according to the Ministry of Commerce. Specifically, FDI in aerospace and equipment manufacturing, services for the commercialization of sci-tech achievements, and electronic and telecommunications equipment manufacturing surged 128.8 percent, 73.3 percent and 35.7 percent, respectively. A total of 52,853 new foreign-invested enterprises were established nationwide during this period, down 1.7 percent year on year, while FDI in actual use stood at 606.93 billion yuan, declining 2.4 percent from a year earlier. China's manufacturing industry attracted 143.04 billion yuan in FDI in this period, while the service sector drew 450.38 billion yuan. During the same period, FDI from Canada, France, Switzerland and the United States grew by 105.7 percent, 35.1 percent, 23.5 percent and 9.6 percent, respectively, with investment via free ports included in these calculations, the ministry revealed. High-tech and high-value-added industries have increasingly become a key focus for foreign investors in China, a report released in September said. Multinational corporations are accelerating the establishment of R&D centers in China, positioning the country as a vital node in their global innovation networks, the report noted. ■

item.title: Xi's APEC speech inspires optimism for new chapter in Asia-Pacific prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
* "If the Asia-Pacific miracle of the past more than three decades was a story of economic growth achieved through openness and cooperation, the next 30 years should be a story of shared prosperity achieved through inclusiveness and win-win cooperation," said South Korean lawmaker Kim Tae-nyeon. * China's proposal to set up cooperation institutions focusing on the digital economy, clean energy and SME cooperation carries great significance and represents a key step in fostering new growth drivers for the Asia-Pacific, said Vitaly Mankevich, president of the Russian-Asian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs. * Georgie Too Hann Huei, COO of the Malaysia-China Business Council in Kuala Lumpur, said China is not only an active practitioner in the digital economy, clean energy and the development of SMEs, but has also accumulated rich experience in these fields, noting that China is now translating its development experience into concrete actions to promote common regional development. SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, calling for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the Asia-Pacific miracle. Experts said Xi's speech at the gathering outlined China's vision for a stronger, more integrated Asia-Pacific community, offering a roadmap for the region to build on the achievements of the past three decades. They also said it could help deepen regional cooperation, create new opportunities for shared development and contribute to peace, stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific and beyond. A SHARED VISION In his Thursday speech, Xi stressed that building an Asia-Pacific community requires solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. These requirements are interconnected and mutually reinforcing, said Herbert Sima, director of the China Studies Center at the University of Auckland, noting they not only provide guidance for economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, but also offer valuable insights into addressing global uncertainties. Solidarity and mutual assistance form the foundation of cooperation, openness and connectivity provide a pathway for development, innovation and progress serve as the driving force for growth, while inclusive development is key to ensuring that cooperation is sustainable and benefits all parties, the expert explained. In his speech, Xi reviewed the achievements of the Asia-Pacific miracle over the past thirty-plus years, stressing the need to adapt to the new realities, take new strides and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation in the face of new opportunities and challenges. Xi's remarks have prompted experts to again reflect on the factors behind the region's remarkable economic growth and the prospects for its future development. Virdika Rizky Utama, executive director of the Jakarta-based think tank PARA Syndicate, said the Asia-Pacific miracle had been driven by open cooperation, trade and investment, and the integration of regional industrial and supply chains. What Xi stressed about building the Asia-Pacific community offered a response to the challenges facing the region and a vision for future cooperation, he said. The expert particularly noted Xi's mention of "open regionalism" in his speech, saying that for developing economies such as Indonesia, the concept means access to broader markets and more convenient connectivity. Tran Thi Hai Yen, a researcher at the Institute for European and Americas Studies at Vietnam Academy of Social Sciences, said Xi's vision comes at a timely moment, which addresses the four practical needs currently facing the Asia-Pacific region. As the rotating chair of APEC this year, she added, China has further clarified the direction of cooperation and underscored the urgency of accelerating joint efforts, helping translate long-term vision into concrete cooperation agendas. History proves that economies can prosper through trade with one another, and Xi reaffirmed the value of trade cooperation and open regionalism, said Craig Emerson, director of the Australia APEC Study Center. Such remarks are highly encouraging at a time when trade liberalization has faced growing skepticism in recent years, noted Emerson, a former Australian trade minister. "If the Asia-Pacific miracle of the past more than three decades was a story of economic growth achieved through openness and cooperation, the next 30 years should be a story of shared prosperity achieved through inclusiveness and win-win cooperation," said South Korean lawmaker Kim Tae-nyeon. "Economies in the Asia-Pacific region differ in terms of economic size, stages of development, history and culture, making the region highly diverse," he said. "This diversity should be regarded as a valuable resource. We should leverage our respective strengths, complement one another's weaknesses and turn these differences into new opportunities for cooperation." BUILDING PILLARS TOGETHER China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, and it is ready to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in building the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community, Xi said in his speech. He also called for strengthening the pillar of economy and trade, upgrading the pillar of connectivity, fostering the pillar of innovation and enhancing the pillar of development. On the importance of connectivity, Alvaro Echeverria, director of the Asia Pacific Chamber of Commerce in Chile, said the call to upgrade the pillar of connectivity was particularly relevant in the current international environment. Greater proximity helps create mutual understanding, Echeverria told Xinhua, saying he welcomes China's call to strengthen connectivity not only through physical infrastructure, but also through continued efforts to promote human development and closer people-to-people exchanges. These efforts could help rebuild trust at a time when the world faces considerable uncertainty and a lack of predictability, while the need for international coordination continues to grow, he added. Xi pointed out that China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, and announced that China will provide 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC's practical cooperation, and to establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges and provide intellectual support. In addition, Xi said that in line with the needs of Asia-Pacific cooperation, China will set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy, and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to contribute to innovation-driven and green growth in the Asia-Pacific. China's proposal to set up cooperation institutions focusing on the digital economy, clean energy and SME cooperation carries great significance and represents a key step in fostering new growth drivers for the Asia-Pacific, said Vitaly Mankevich, president of the Russian-Asian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs. "As a recognized technology leader in the digital economy, clean energy and related sectors, China can use these cooperation bodies to advance pragmatic cooperation among Asia-Pacific economies and build science and technology innovation partnerships," Mankevich said. Georgie Too Hann Huei, COO of the Malaysia-China Business Council in Kuala Lumpur, said China is not only an active practitioner in the digital economy, clean energy and the development of SMEs, but has also accumulated rich experience in these fields, noting that China is now translating its development experience into concrete actions to promote common regional development.
